title: Elder Tissa: “As if struck by a sword, As if his head were on fire, Mindful, a monk should go forth, Abandoning sensual lust.”
content:
Elder Tissa:
“As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning sensual lust.”

title: “Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire…
content: “Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire their welfare, benefit, security refers to Māra the Evil One. Monks, the dangerous path refers to the wrong eightfold path – wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration. Monks, the male decoy refers to delight and greed. Monks, the female decoy refers to ignorance. Monks, the man who desires their welfare, benefit, security refers to the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. The safe, secure path leading to happiness refers to the Noble Eightfold Path – right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.”

title: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be…
content: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the present is painful, very hot, very feverish. And these beings who have not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures, being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, with corrupt faculties, perceive as pleasure that which is actually painful contact with sensual pleasures.”

title: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it…
content: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it as a killer, see it as being killed, see it as a disease, see it as a boil, see it as a dart, see it as misery, see it as its own misery. One who sees form thus sees rightly.”

title: Behold this adorned appearance, With jewels and earrings, A skeleton covered by skin, Made beautiful by clothes.
content:
Behold this adorned appearance,
With jewels and earrings,
A skeleton covered by skin,
Made beautiful by clothes.

title: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with…
content: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. After some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of forms, he abandons craving for forms, removes the fever for forms, and dwells with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful.”

title: “Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three…
content:
“Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three kinds of craving.

Bound by the bondage of craving,
Their minds attached to becoming and non-becoming,
Bound by Māra’s bondage,
Those beings are not secure from bondage.
They go on in the wandering,
Gone to birth and death.

But those who have abandoned craving,
Free from craving for becoming and non-becoming,
Having reached the far shore,
In this very world, they have attained
The destruction of the defilements.”

title: The Blessed One: “Seeing craving, aversion, and lust, There is no desire for sexual intercourse. What is this, so full of urine and feces? I…
content:
The Blessed One:
“Seeing craving, aversion, and lust,
There is no desire for sexual intercourse.
What is this, so full of urine and feces?
I would not wish even to touch it with my foot.”

title: “For the most part, monks, beings find pleasure in sensual pleasures. But a clansman who has set aside the sickle and the carrying-pole, gone forth…
content: “For the most part, monks, beings find pleasure in sensual pleasures. But a clansman who has set aside the sickle and the carrying-pole, gone forth from the household life into homelessness, is justifiably called ‘a clansman who has gone forth out of faith.’ Why is that? Sensual pleasures are found with youth, these sensual pleasures or others. And, monks, low sensual pleasures, middling sensual pleasures, and supreme sensual pleasures — all are classed as sensual pleasures.”

title: “Monks, sensual pleasures are impermanent, empty, false, of a delusive nature. Monks, this is the mere greeting of a fool built upon deception. Sensual pleasures…
content: “Monks, sensual pleasures are impermanent, empty, false, of a delusive nature. Monks, this is the mere greeting of a fool built upon deception. Sensual pleasures present and future, perceptions of sensual pleasure present and future — both belong to Māra’s realm, Māra’s domain, Māra’s bait, Māra’s food.”
